clue.text: Subject inspiring reverence primarily, one circling the globe

indicators.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so the subject takes a letter into itself

parts.note: a subject of discussion is a topic

indicators.note: primarily points to the opening letter of the word reverence

explanation.surface: A theme that fills someone with awe, alongside a mention of a world traveller.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tropics of Cancer and Capricorn are lines of latitude running all the way around the Earth.

clue.text: Around pit, person keeping busy, as boss about

indicators.note: around tells us the busy person's word wraps itself about the pit's word

parts.note: someone who keeps busy doing things is a doer
a pit is a mine, as in a coal pit

explanation.surface: A busy worker at a colliery throws their weight around like a manager.
explanation.definitionFit: To domineer is to act overbearingly, ordering others around as a bossy person does.

clue.text: Part of orchestra that's supersonic when vibrating

indicators.note: vibrating suggests the letters of supersonic shaking about into a new order

explanation.surface: An orchestral section loud enough to break the sound barrier when it gets going.
explanation.definitionFit: The drums, cymbals and other struck instruments form a named section of the orchestra.

clue.text: Stumble after a few drinks, going one way then the other

definitions.text: going one way then the other

indicators.note: after places the stumble's word behind the drinks' word

parts.note: a round is a set of drinks bought for a group
to stumble is to trip

explanation.surface: Someone tripping up after a few drinks, lurching this way and that.
explanation.definitionFit: A journey out and back again is a there-and-back trip, travelling one direction then returning.

clue.text: Dreary poet sent up

indicators.note: in a down clue, sent up means the poet's word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a bard is a poet

explanation.surface: A dull poet being mocked or satirised.
explanation.definitionFit: Drab and dreary are synonyms: both describe something dull and lacking colour or interest.

clue.text: This person is overlooking agreement in effect

indicators.note: in a down clue, overlooking puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: the setter speaking of themselves: I'm
a pact is an agreement

explanation.surface: Someone admitting they are ignoring a deal that is currently in force.
explanation.definitionFit: An impact is the effect or influence that something has.

clue.text: King has designed a winter scarf, say

parts.note: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

indicators.note: designed suggests the letters of a winter being fashioned into a new shape

explanation.surface: A monarch has created a scarf for the cold season.
explanation.definitionFit: A scarf is one example of a woollen garment made by knitting.

clue.text: Violent protesters initially roaring 'Tories out'

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of roaring
out here means disordered, so the letters of Tories are rearranged

explanation.surface: An angry crowd shouting for the Conservatives to be thrown out of power.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who riot are people protesting with violence in the streets.

clue.text: Genesis character in paradise then

indicators.note: in tells us the character sits inside the words paradise then, spanning both

explanation.surface: A figure from the Book of Genesis, living in Eden at that time.
explanation.definitionFit: Seth is the third son of Adam and Eve, named in the Book of Genesis.

clue.text: Preserving energy, Romans relaxed — slaves driving galley, maybe

indicators.note: preserving means keeping something held inside, so the rearranged Romans hold the energy letter
relaxed suggests the letters of Romans loosened into a different order

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Easy-going Romans conserve their strength while slaves power the galley.
explanation.definitionFit: Galley slaves propelled the ship by rowing, so they were rowers pulling the oars.

clue.text: Voting system not nice, unfortunately, in US university

parts.note: PR stands for proportional representation, an electoral system

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests the letters of not nice have gone wrong and are jumbled

explanation.surface: Complaints about an unpleasant electoral method used at an American college.
explanation.definitionFit: Princeton is an Ivy League university in New Jersey.

clue.text: Criticise or clap?

definitions.meaning: to criticise harshly is to ..., as in ... a policy
a clap of thunder is a loud explosive noise

explanation.surface: Should one condemn a performance or applaud it?
explanation.definitionFit: One word covers both a severe verbal attack and a sudden loud bang like a thunderclap.

clue.text: Where men are on board ship beside revolutionary

indicators.note: beside places the ship's letters next to the revolutionary

parts.note: Che Guevara is the classic crossword revolutionary
SS is the abbreviation for steamship

explanation.surface: A rebel stands next to a vessel, with sailors on deck.
explanation.definitionFit: Chessmen are the pieces set out on a chessboard, so the game is where those men sit.

clue.text: Snack to put with something sparkling and European

parts.note: Asti is a sparkling Italian wine

explanation.surface: A light bite to go with a glass of fizz and something continental.
explanation.definitionFit: A toastie is a toasted sandwich, a popular light snack in Britain.

clue.text: A story on country producing hostility

parts.note: a story can mean a fib, a lie
a country is a nation

explanation.surface: A tale about a nation that stirs up bad feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Alienation is estrangement, a turning away of goodwill that becomes unfriendliness.

clue.text: Seriously rolling in the hay perhaps, ear bitten

indicators.note: the ear is bitten, held between the teeth of the other piece and so sitting inside it

parts.note: a nest may be made of hay, so being in the hay could be being in a nest
taken as written

explanation.surface: A romp in the hay turns serious when someone nibbles an ear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rolling in the hay' reads as romance, but the hay is what a bird's nest is made of; 'bitten' means the ear is held inside that piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To do something in earnest is to do it seriously and sincerely, an idiom for meaning it.

clue.text: I'm so interfering, travelling as a politician?

indicators.note: travelling suggests the letters of I'm so interfering moving about into a new order

explanation.surface: A meddling official who jets around the world admits the habit.
explanation.definitionFit: The government minister responsible for overseas affairs is a senior politician who travels abroad.

clue.text: Perfect female, unruly

parts.note: unruly means lawless, ignoring rules

explanation.surface: A woman who is ideal yet ungovernable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something perfect has no defects at all, without a single blemish.

clue.text: Freshwater reptile bringing one salmon up in ten

indicators.note: in tells us the reversed pieces go inside the word ten
in a down clue, up means one and salmon are read from bottom to top

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
a parr is a young salmon

explanation.surface: An aquatic creature arriving with a single fish among ten.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrapin is a small turtle that lives in fresh water, a reptile.

clue.text: Country folk appearing in operatic piece

indicators.note: appearing in means the folk's word is placed inside the operatic piece

parts.note: an aria is a solo song in an opera
folk are people, men

explanation.surface: Country people performing in an opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Armenia is a nation in the South Caucasus region.

clue.text: Two relatives meeting tomorrow in Madrid?

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother, one relative
two signals a second relative, nana being a grandmother

explanation.surface: A pair of family members arranging to get together the next day in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Mañana is Spanish for tomorrow, with the question mark marking this as an example of Spanish usage.

clue.text: Bottle — optic possibly applied to it?

definitions.meaning: bottle is British slang for courage or daring
the optic ... is the one serving the eye, so optic is a word that can be applied to it

explanation.surface: A spirit bottle with its pub measuring dispenser fitted on top.
explanation.walkthrough: In a British pub an optic is the measuring device fixed upside down on a spirits bottle, which is the misleading picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Courage and the optic nerve share one word: daring and the fibre linking eye to brain.

clue.text: Go green, changing policy finally

indicators.note: changing suggests the letters of green are altered into another order
finally points to the closing letter of policy

explanation.surface: An exhortation to become environmentally friendly by at last altering policy.
explanation.definitionFit: Go means vigour or drive, as in full of go, which is the same as vitality.

clue.text: A grand queen going to a city in India

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand; that the clue's opening words a grand also contain the city is a coincidence, as the setter builds it piece by piece
R is from Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A splendid queen travelling to an Indian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Agra is a city in Uttar Pradesh, home of the Taj Mahal.

clue.text: Old communist figure turning back on Left

indicators.note: turning back means the figure's word is read in reverse

parts.note: a figure can be a number, here nine

explanation.surface: A former communist leader who has turned his back on the political left.
explanation.definitionFit: Vladimir Ilyich, leader of the 1917 Bolshevik revolution, was the founding Soviet communist.

clue.text: Want to work hard, you announce?

indicators.note: you announce means the word is spoken, so we go by its sound not its spelling

parts.note: to knead is to work dough hard with the hands

explanation.surface: Someone declaring that they wish to put in a hard day's graft.
explanation.definitionFit: To want something is to require it, a lack that must be met.

clue.text: Dreadful experience being near horse nursing temperature

indicators.note: nursing means holding something close inside, so the temperature letter is held within

parts.note: nigh is an old word for near
a mare is a female horse

explanation.surface: Being close to a horse running a fever.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrifying ordeal is often called a bad dream, as in the trip was a total horror.

clue.text: Boy captures the work of Shakespeare, for example

definitions.text: the work of Shakespeare, for example

parts.note: a boy is a son
to net is to catch, so captures gives nets

explanation.surface: A lad gets hold of Shakespeare's writings.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare wrote 154 fourteen-line poems, an example of his work.

clue.text: Loving a swindle, gang

parts.note: a do is slang for a swindle or con
a ring is a gang of criminals

explanation.surface: Fond of a scam and a criminal crew.
explanation.definitionFit: Doting and worshipping are the same as being devoted and affectionate.
